en-US.author: Jean-Pierre Bergamin
en-US.description: Command-line emulator of classic HP calculators
en-US.longDescription: saturnus emulates the HP 48SX, 48GX, 49G, 38G, 39G, 40G, 42S, 27S, 17BII, 17B, 28S and 19BII from their own ROMs. The command line runs a calculator without a window: it presses keys listed in a text file, saves the screen as text or a PNG, serves the serial port and looks up the built-in commands. No ROM is included.
en-US.name: saturnus (command line)
en-US.releaseNotes:
Download the desktop app
- Mac (Apple silicon): saturnus_0.10.3_aarch64.dmg
- Windows (Intel or AMD): saturnus_0.10.3_x64-setup.exe
- Windows on ARM: saturnus_0.10.3_arm64-setup.exe
The Windows installers are not signed yet: if Windows says "Windows protected your PC", click "More info", then "Run anyway".
Linux, the .msi installers, the command-line tools and satx: see Assets at the end of this page.
saturnus 0.10.3 fixes what two code reviews found: quitting the desktop app
now saves, and failed writes, backups and directory changes clean up after
themselves.

Get it
- On the web, nothing to install: https://ractive.ch/saturnus/app/
  (Chrome or Edge for a serial cable; every browser for the emulated
  calculator).
- The desktop app saturnus_0.10.3_… (on Linux saturnus-app), with
  a -SHA256SUMS file beside them:
  - macOS, Apple silicon: .dmg, signed and notarised, or brew trust --cask ractive/tap/saturnus-app once, then brew install --cask ractive/tap/saturnus-app;
  - Windows: .msi or -setup.exe for x86_64 (x64) and ARM (arm64);
  - Linux: .deb, .rpm or .AppImage for x86_64 (amd64, x86_64)
    and ARM (arm64, aarch64). Add yourself to the dialout group to
    use a serial port.
- The command-line tools saturnus and satx: cargo install,
  Homebrew ractive/tap, Scoop ractive, or the archives and Linux
  packages below.
- Libraries on crates.io, all at 0.10.3.

Desktop app and web page
- Quitting the desktop app saves the calculator. Cmd+Q on a Mac now
  saves an unsaved change, as closing the window always did.
- A fresh start keeps what it should. A ROM that doesn't boot no longer
  deletes the kept state. A ROM that boots as another model reads or clears
  that model's state, not the one you asked for.
- A failed save leaves the old file. The desktop app writes saved files
  and its AI access setting to the side, then moves them into place.

satx and Files
- A variable name with @ is refused. The calculator reads @ as the
  start of a comment, so satx and Files no longer take such a name.
- A directory that isn't there changes nothing. satx --dir, satx ls PATH and the REPL's :cd and :ls leave the calculator where it was
  when a name in the path is missing, not part of the way down it.
  satx xserv goes back to HOME, as XSERV can't say where it was.
- A backup that fails no longer leaves its copies behind. satx backup
  and Files remove the copy in port 0 when the calculator runs out of
  memory, and a backup of an emulated calculator whose server stops
  answering removes what it made. A port copy it can't be sure of stays,
  and the error says so.
- Files replaces a variable with a long name. The swap goes out as three
  commands when it doesn't fit in one packet. A name too long even for that
  is refused, and the old variable stays.
- satx get --force replaces a file whole. A failed write leaves the
  old file, and a new file it could not finish is removed. In a directory
  where satx can't create a file, --force still writes in place, so a
  failed write there loses the old content.
- Smaller fixes. satx rm X X deletes X once instead of failing on the
  second. satx repl --json sends nothing more once its reader has closed.

Emulator
- A transfer that fails lets go of a key it held down.
- A UART break that is looped back and let go early leaves the receiver
  idle (inferred: the manual covers a full break only).
